feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: What's next after a brutal stock plunge we might have seen coming
entry.summary: Stocks tanked this week as investors grew wary of tech investments that have seen years of growth. NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Katie Martin of the Financial Times about the global ripple effects.

entry.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.

entry.title: Google employees protest AI in schools policy
entry.summary: More than 550 Google employees signed a petition to allow schools access to Search without AI. Parents and educators protested outside Google offices in 6 cities last week for the same ask.

entry.title: Deadlocked again? U.N. climate talks in Turkey go into overtime
entry.summary: United Nations climate talks are heading into super overtime this weekend in Turkey. Negotiations were supposed to wrap up Friday but talks have spilled into a second night.

entry.title: Inside a Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack release party in Miami
entry.summary: Music is a major part of the video game Grand Theft Auto. The latest release, Grand Theft Auto VI comes with its own carefully crafted soundtrack played on radio stations inside the game. The game is based in the fictional Vice City, based on Miami, Florida. WLRN's Alyssa Ramos went to a soundtrack release party to learn more about how the music of GTA VI captures Miami's vibe.

entry.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
entry.summary: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.

entry.title: Fuschia Dunlop's Sichuan cooking tips
entry.summary: Fuschia Dunlop, author and Sichuan food celebrity, shows NPR's Rob Schmitz how to make 'strange flavor sauce' and talks about bringing Sichuan cooking to people outside and inside China.

entry.title: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village
entry.summary: In Southern Lebanon, the Army is taking over after Israeli forces withdraw. One grieving family returns to their village to find almost everything in their house destroyed.

entry.title: NEA announces 2027 Jazz Masters class
entry.summary: The National Endowment for the Arts has named Terry Gibbs, Rufus Reid, Larry Ridley, Harvey Mason and John Edward Hasse as the newest musicians and advocates to receive the highest federal jazz honor.

entry.title: Tech stocks end the week on a down note, despite Anthropic's mega-IPO
entry.summary: The stock market is ending the week down despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO and a strong Nvidia earnings report, largely thanks to investor jitters about the future of AI.
